questions.question: What is antimony, and which forms matter?
questions.answer: Antimony (Sb) is a metalloid, and its forms are not the same hazard. Trivalent antimony, which includes antimony trioxide and antimony potassium tartrate, is treated differently from pentavalent antimony. IARC Monograph Volume 131, announced on 5 May 2023, classifies trivalent antimony as Group 2A (probably carcinogenic to humans) and pentavalent antimony as Group 3 (not classifiable). Antimony trioxide was Group 2B in the 1989 evaluation. Because antimony trioxide is trivalent, it falls inside the 2023 classification, which covers the trivalent class rather than a separate line that names only the oxide.

questions.question: How do people come into contact with antimony?
questions.answer: IARC lists uses in flame retardants, plastics, brake pads, glass, ceramics, and lead alloys. For water, WHO's drinking-water fact sheet treats plumbing and fittings as the common source and states that drinking-water concentrations appear to be below 5 µg/L. In Romania, [[sources/ungureanu2022-bottled-water-toxic-elements|Ungureanu and colleagues 2022]] measured bottled-water antimony from below 0.07 µg/L to a printed maximum of 0.64 ± 6.85 µg/L. [[sources/stone2021-wa-metals-childrens-consumer-products|Washington Ecology]] measured tens of ppm of antimony in screened baby-wipe, bib, and clothing components, but those figures come from a prioritized screen, not a random market mean. Skin contact is the least documented route. OECD and OEHHA summarize an unpublished in vitro dermal study at 0.26 percent, and OEHHA also prints 0.14 percent at a higher dose. That is not an absorption fraction for a wipe or a textile, and the primary report was not examined.

questions.question: What are the intake values and water limits for antimony?
questions.answer: WHO's tolerable daily intake is 6 µg/kg body weight, from a NOAEL of 6.0 mg/kg/day in a 90-day rat study of potassium antimony tartrate and an uncertainty factor of 1000, and its drinking-water guideline is 0.02 mg/L. ATSDR's 2019 intermediate oral minimal risk level is 0.0006 mg Sb/kg/day, because ATSDR took a much lower NOAEL (0.06 mg Sb/kg/day) from the same study, and there is no chronic oral minimal risk level. For drinking water, the U.S. EPA maximum contaminant level is 0.006 mg/L, and OEHHA's 2016 public health goal is 1 ppb, from a BMDL of 0.14 mg/kg-day and an uncertainty factor of 1,000. These values answer different questions and are not averaged. The EPA IRIS oral reference dose was not examined for this page, so it is not stated.

questions.question: Do toy, food-contact, and cosmetic limits mean the same thing?
questions.answer: No. Each is written on a different basis. EU 10/2011 sets a specific migration limit of 0.04 mg/kg into food from plastic. EN 71-3 sets soluble toy migration at 45, 11.3, and 560 mg/kg of toy material for Categories I, II, and III. Health Canada's cosmetic guidance is 5 ppm in a finished cosmetic, and it is guidance, not a wipe regulation. EU cosmetics law prohibits antimony and its compounds as ingredients (Annex II, entry 40) and sets no trace ppm in Article 17. A drinking-water limit cannot be copied onto a textile or a wipe either. The OEKO-TEX record in this corpus is a wastewater limit of 100 µg/L, not an extractable limit in a finished article.

questions.question: What is known about antimony and microbes?
questions.answer: The evidence is mostly in vitro, animal, and observational. In vitro, Li and colleagues 2017 showed that bacterial proteins shared with arsenic (AnoA, AioAB, ArsB, Acr3, GlpF) oxidize, efflux, or take up Sb(III). Deng and colleagues 2021, a review, state that the genes required for microbial antimony methylation are still unknown. Engrola and colleagues 2023 found antimonite in the arsenite-oxidase active site and state that Sb(III) is oxidized about 6,500 times more slowly than As(III). In mice, Wu and colleagues 2025 found gut and bile-acid changes after a high gavage dose of potassium antimony tartrate (10 mg/kg), which is not a consumer-product dose. In hospitalized infants, Yan and colleagues 2025 report a negative association between serum antimony and the Chao1 diversity index, without a single-metal beta in the main text. In saliva, Davis and colleagues 2020 associated antimony with oral taxa and decayed teeth. Zeldin and colleagues 2023 associated antimony air-release inventories with atopic dermatitis billing in one U.S. region and, in vitro, showed effects on a skin commensal and a neuronal itch receptor. That is not a diaper-area cohort, and the printed billing code does not match the title.
